sections.html:
The Register of Deeds sits on the ground-level floor of the Martin County Governmental Building in Williamston. Land records there start in 1771. Easements, agreements, assignments, releases, plats, deeds and deeds of trust are all recorded at this counter, with an index for each kind and a separate index for plats.

Uniform commercial code statements join the real estate books too, a practice dating to July 1, 2001. The office also files military discharge papers (DD-214), assumed business name, partnership and incorporation instruments, and gives oaths to notaries.

A title searcher will find whatever sits in these books, so look first. If something odd turns up, such as an easement or an unreleased lien, ask the office about it before you list.

Deeds are searchable at martinrod.org, with records back to 1771. A separate online service takes vital record orders.

If you inherited the house or have owned it for decades, an hour in the index is time well spent.

  • Search under your name and under the previous owner's name.
  • Match the legal description on the latest deed to the tax record.
  • Flag any old deed of trust that has no release recorded behind it.
  • Note any plat or state right of way plan that touches the lot.

The county's fee sheet follows the statewide schedule, and amounts can change. Call about the total before you mail a payment, and write money orders to Martin County Register of Deeds.

Selected Martin County recording charges
ServiceCharge
Deed or other instrument, pages 1 to 15$26
Pages beyond 15$4 each
Deed of trust, pages 1 to 35$64
Plat or map (18 x 24)$21.00 a page
State right of way plans$21.00 first page, $5.00 after

Uncertified photocopy$0.25 a page
Deed excise tax$2.00 per $1000 of price

Extra instrument within one document$10.00 each

A re-recorded instrument costs the same as the original unless pages were added, and each added page is $4.

Any paper signed on or after July 1, 2002 must follow the layout rules in G.S. 161-10, or the office tacks $25.00 onto the recording charge.

  • Letter or legal paper, 8 1/2 inches wide.
  • A blank three-inch band across the top of page one and half-inch margins elsewhere.
  • Black on white, type no smaller than 9 points, printed on one face.
  • The words naming the instrument type, printed above everything else on page one.

Hand-inked blanks and corrections are allowed, and exhibits follow the same rules. The signing date decides which standard applies, not the arrival date.

This one is the seller's. Martin County's sheet words the rate as $2.00 per $1000 of purchase price; the statute words it as $1.00 per $500, with a partial block rounded up.

Payment comes at filing. The money is divided between the county general fund and the state, and the county can keep 2 percent of the state's share.

Your settlement statement shows the exact dollars in the seller's column. Staff hold the deed until the tax is in.

sections.h2: Why filing order matters on a Williamston sale
sections.html:
A deed, an option, a lease longer than three years or a right of first refusal protects its holder against lien creditors and paying purchasers only after it is registered (G.S. 47-18). For land in this county, registration happens in Williamston no matter where the owner lives.

Suppose a creditor files a judgment an hour before your buyer's deed goes in. The buyer can end up second in line. Attorneys head this off by filing the moment funds are confirmed.

  • Mail or deliver the signed deed with any lender release in a single packet.
  • Include a check covering fee and tax.
  • Get the book and page reference after recording.

sections.h2: Steps from signed deed to recorded deed
sections.html:
Nearly every Martin County sale moves along this short path, cash sales included.

  • The attorney or title company checks the old deed, the legal description and the payoff letters for any loan on the house.
  • The seller signs in front of a notary.
  • The packet, with a check for the fee and the tax, goes to Williamston. Page count sets the fee, so ask the office to total it when a deed runs long.
  • Staff stamp the time, index the deed and hand back the book and page reference.
  • Any lender release follows. It costs nothing to record, but someone has to make sure the lender actually sends it.

With no lender underwriting in the way, a cash sale often leaves the records as the one thing to clear. If an old deed of trust shows up with no release after it, start that request with the lender right away, since the lender's response time sets the pace.

The same counter issues marriage licenses and certified vital records, and heirs selling an inherited house often need the latter. A certified copy of a birth, death or marriage record costs $10.00, and the county limits who may request one: the person named, close family members, an authorized agent or attorney, or anyone who can prove a legal need tied to a personal or property right.

An executor or heir usually brings proof of the relationship or a document showing legal authority. Uncertified copies are open to the public at $0.25 a page.

sections.h2: Tax bills, due dates and interest
sections.html:
Recording a deed does not change the tax bill. Real and personal property bills are mailed in July or August and fall due September 1. You can pay with no interest through January 5. When that day lands on a weekend or holiday, the cutoff slides to the next business day.

On January 6 a 2 percent penalty kicks in, and three-fourths of one percent more is added each month afterward. Between March 1 and June 30 the collector must run unpaid real estate tax in the local newspaper, and the delinquent owner is charged for the notice.

Visit the collector at 305 East Main Street, Room 125 (8 AM to 5 PM on weekdays) or phone 252-789-4360. A written payoff figure lets the attorney deduct the bill from your proceeds at the table.

Population was about 21,601 in mid-2025, a 2.0 percent drop from April 2020, spread across 11,071 housing units. For 2020 to 2024 the owner-occupied rate was 66.8 percent and the median home value $109,700.

With values this modest, deferred repairs can make a traditional lender balk. A cash buyer will take the house in its present state, repairs untouched, and close as soon as title is clear. Have your attorney run the land records early so any uncancelled deed of trust gets released before closing.

faqs.q: Where is the Martin County register of deeds?
faqs.a: In the Martin County Governmental Building in Williamston, on the first floor. The county prints (252) 789-4320 for record questions.

faqs.q: How far back do Martin County land records go?
faqs.a: To 1771. The index of recorded instruments starts that year, and deeds are searchable at martinrod.org.

faqs.q: What is the Martin County fee for a deed of trust?
faqs.a: $64 through page 35, plus $4 per additional page or fraction. A plain deed costs $26 through page 15.

faqs.q: Does Martin County charge for recording a mortgage satisfaction?
faqs.a: No. Cancellations, certificates of satisfaction and notices of satisfaction all carry no fee.

faqs.q: Who pays Martin County's deed excise tax?
faqs.a: The seller, at $2.00 per $1000 of price, collected as the deed is filed.
